summary: Bulk-review hardening: POST /api/tags/bulk, per-chunk coverage, remaining-pending reconciliation
description:
Driver report from the blavatsky-sd tag-review loop (~11k verdicts queued via individual POST /api/tags/:id/action calls from Python). A client-side bug (reasoning lines comment-converted inside a dict literal) silently dropped ~863 verdicts across five batches; the API reported success each time and nothing surfaced the drift until the cursor stopped matching.

Requested changes, priority order:
1. POST /api/tags/bulk accepting [{target_id, action}], returning {queued, skipped, unknown_ids} — kills per-tag HTTP loops and makes client/server counts reconcile in one response.
2. Per-chunk coverage in GET /api/chunks (pending_total vs queued per chunk) so an under-queued batch is visible on the next fetch.
3. Include remaining_pending_in_text (or by_chunk coverage) in action responses and/or /api/apply/preview so reconciliation is a comparison, not archaeology.
4. Docs note recommending a JSONL working file as source of truth for scripted bulk review, uploaded by a dumb reader, rather than building the payload in code.
